scene.title: Why water is bent
scene.summary: Two lone pairs on oxygen repel the H‑O bonds, compressing the H‑O‑H angle to 104.5° and giving water its bent shape.

beats.title: Water molecule appears
beats.narration: The H₂O molecule is shown with two hydrogens bonded to oxygen.

beats.title: Lone pairs on oxygen
beats.narration: Oxygen holds two lone pairs that are drawn as a label above it.

beats.title: Predict the bond angle
beats.narration: Why is the H‑O‑H angle smaller than the tetrahedral 109.5°?

check.question: What causes the reduced angle?
check.explain: Lone‑pair‑lone‑pair repulsion pushes the bonds closer together.

beats.title: Angle shown
beats.narration: The H‑O‑H angle is drawn as 104.5°, illustrating the bend caused by the lone pairs.

beats.title: Takeaway
beats.narration: The two lone pairs compress the bond angle to 104.5°, so water has a bent molecular shape.
